prompt:
Minecraft builder reference sheet, landscape 3:2. Vanilla Minecraft blocks only, crisp voxel style, plain light background, no characters or animals. Two views side by side: LEFT a straight-on north front elevation, strictly orthographic; RIGHT a north three-quarter view of the same estate at the same scale. Skilled human builder quality: real massing and depth, projecting galleries and recessed framed openings, actual stair/slab roof verges, eaves and ridge, fence balustrades, trapdoor shutters, lanterns. Show the complete 96 x 96 estate in each panel, with the mansion readable and the right view elevated enough to reveal grounds and river behind it. No inset views.
Site: A grand antebellum Greek Revival plantation estate on a river, seen from the north. A straight gravel drive runs from white gate piers with lanterns at the road, under an allee of eight huge spreading live oaks whose dark crowns meet overhead and drip with Spanish moss represented by vine and hanging_roots, to an oval gravel forecourt around a lawn island with a decorated_pot urn. Behind it stands the mansion, broad and symmetrical: a brilliant white two-storey block on a red-brick raised base with arched iron_bars vents. Across its whole front, exactly eight colossal white fluted quartz_pillar columns with block-built Ionic capitals rise the full two storeys. They carry a deep double gallery: a white-floored ground porch reached by wide smooth_quartz_stairs, and an upper porch with white birch_fence balustrades between columns. A plain white entablature and dentilled quartz cornice run above. One low, wide dark-slate hip roof has three white gabled dormers on the front, two on the back, and four red-brick chimneys with dark bands and stepped caps. Behind the columns, tall floor-length glass_pane windows hang between near-black dark_oak_trapdoor shutters. In the centre of each floor is a dark double dark_oak_door with glass sidelights and transom in a white pillared surround. A slate-hipped rear wing with a tall arched Palladian window and slim-columned back porch faces a lawn running down to a sand bank, brown-green river water and spruce landing dock with lanterns. To the west (left in north elevation) are a formal parterre of dark boxwood dark_oak_leaves hedges, flower beds and spruce_leaves cone topiaries around a white quartz fountain, a white-framed glass greenhouse on a brick dwarf wall, and an octagonal white gazebo with a dark pointed cap on the riverbank. To the east are a red-brick carriage house with white quoins, three arched carriage doors and a white lantern cupola on its slate hip, and a little white guest cottage with its own four-column porch under a slate hip. Pink cherry trees and magnolias represented by flowering_azalea_leaves dot lawns; lantern posts line every path.
Dimensions: estate 96 x 96 blocks; mansion including gallery 46 blocks wide x 41 blocks deep including rear wing, two tall storeys plus low hip roof, about 30 blocks high.

Permitted functional/decor blocks: barrel, chest, smoker, furnace, campfire, cauldron, water_cauldron, flower_pot, decorated_pot, candle, iron_chain, white_bed, red_bed, lectern, loom, composter, anvil, jukebox, bell, ladder, hay_block, lightning_rod, white_wool, red_wool, bookshelf. Use only where actually needed; do not expose indoor furnishings just to show the inventory.
All forms must be buildable block geometry, including stepped arches and block-built Ionic capitals; no smooth sculpted classical details. Soft neutral daylight, sharp readable textures, no cinematic effects.
changes: Generated with the built-in image_gen tool and copied unchanged to concept.png in the current directory.
The roles retain the complete planned palette. Exact block identities cannot be proven from raster artwork; no additional material is confidently identifiable.
The objects list includes the functional and decor blocks drawn as icons in the bottom inventory key. Most are not visibly placed in the estate; lanterns and planted urns are visible in the scene.
The left panel is an elevated frontal view rather than a straight-on orthographic elevation. Equal scale between panels is not established.

The mansion appears to have six colossal front columns rather than eight. Their fluting, capitals and some railings use fine sculptural detail that is not clearly reproducible with vanilla block shapes.
The rear wing has a tall, prominent roof and gabled Palladian-window facade instead of a subordinate slate-hipped wing. Its slim-columned back porch is not clearly shown.

White perimeter fencing, dark entrance gates, a paved roadside strip and additional roof ornaments have been added.
